bull.probability_evidence: Bull case: LVS holds one of six Macao concessions (to Dec 2032) and one of two Singapore licences (duopoly protected to Jan 2031) — statutory scarcity, not brand/scale — while TTM ROIC is 19.8%, FCF margin 19.7% and FCF yield 11.65%, with LVS still ~23% below peer P/E and EV/EBITDA medians (research/LVS/2026-10-08.md §2-3; research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md bull case).

target_price_12m.cite: research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.bull.target_price_12m, basis: P/E re-rates 13.9x→18.0x peer median on flat TTM earnings

target_band.cite: Half the spread between the P/E-based target (46.37: 18.0x peer P/E vs 13.9x current [RA,P:WYNN,P:MGM,P:MLCO]) and the EV/EBITDA-based target (46.65: 9.9x peer EV/EBITDA vs 7.6x current, same sources) — factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table, both anchors showing LVS cheap vs peers in the same direction

base.probability_evidence: Base case: the evaluator's rationale finds the probability-weighted 12m value roughly equal to the current price — quality/licence strengths are offset by an unexplained 31.5% 12m drawdown and LVS trading pricier than peers on P/FCF (8.6x vs 5.0x) and EV/Sales (2.6x vs 2.0x); conviction scored 3/5, 'good, not compelling' (research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md decision rationale; factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table).

target_price_12m.cite: research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.base.target_price_12m, basis: P/E holds at 13.9x while 6.01% YoY share reduction [ST] lifts per-share earnings

target_band.cite: No disagreement across valuation anchors for this mechanism: holding either P/E (13.9x) or P/FCF (8.6x) flat while per-share value grows by the same 6.01% YoY buyback-driven factor [factsheet-2026-10-08.md 'Other' table, ST] gives an identical 38.10 target either way, so the band is 0.

bear.probability_evidence: Bear case: Macao EBITDA was hit by low VIP hold and renovations remove ~400-500 keys/quarter into 2027; LVS already trades above peers on P/FCF (8.6x vs 5.0x) and EV/Sales (2.6x vs 2.0x), leaving no valuation cushion, while 2.57x net debt/EBITDA and $787m of Q2 2026 buybacks leave little balance-sheet slack if EBITDA slips (research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md bear case; research/LVS/2026-10-08.md §2,§5).

target_price_12m.cite: research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md Decision JSON scenarios.bear.target_price_12m, basis: P/FCF de-rates 8.6x→5.0x peer median

target_band.cite: Half the spread between the P/FCF-based target (20.82: de-rating 8.6x to the 5.0x peer P/FCF [RA,P:WYNN,P:MGM,P:MLCO]) and the EV/Sales-based target (27.55: de-rating 2.6x to the 2.0x peer EV/Sales, same sources) — factsheet-2026-10-08.md Valuation table shows LVS trading above peers on both of these multiples, the largest documented anchor disagreement

expected_12m_move.cite: Mixed/conflicting SPY headlines as of 2026-10-07 — record highs led by tech (CNBC, WSJ, Bloomberg) alongside a broader sell-off underneath, elevated Treasury yields pressuring stocks (TipRanks) and a large bearish put-spread trade (CNBC) — no net directional read (research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json factor_news.SPY).

Bond-market headlines through 2026-10-07 are predominantly one-directional — 'Global Bond Markets Sell Off' (Barrons), 'The Bond Rout Is Deepening' (WSJ), 'US Benchmark 10-Year Bond Yields Hit Highest Level Since 2002' (Bloomberg), yields 'resumed their climb' (Reuters) — consistent with the macro overlay's US 10y real yield (DFII10) rising to 2.91% (+0.61pp over 3m) and its macro_bear chain ('real yields keep climbing'); rising yields imply IEF price pressure, kept modest given the brief early-Oct pullback also reported (ETF Trends) (research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json factor_news.IEF; research/LVS/2026-10-08-macro.md).

jumps.name: Q3 2026 earnings surprise (Oct 21, 2026)
jumps.reason: LVS reports Q3 2026 earnings on Oct 21, 2026, two weeks after this valuation date; the bear case flags that results 'could reset the base,' and quarterly prints have produced double-digit weekly moves repeatedly over the regression window (e.g. Q3 2025 +18.7%, Q4 2025 -12.0%, Q2 2022 +12.9%).
jumps.cite: research/LVS/factsheet-2026-10-08.md Price section ('Next earnings date Oct 21, 2026'); research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md bear case ('Earnings on Oct 21 could reset the base [Guessing]')

annual_probability.cite: 3 of the last 20 quarterly earnings weeks in research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues.event_weeks moved ≥12% (|move|): +12.9% (2022-07-18), +18.7% (2025-10-20), -12.0% (2026-01-26) — a 15% per-quarter base rate implies 1-(1-0.15)^4 ≈ 48% chance of at least one such move across the 4 quarterly prints in the next 12 months

impact.cite: Matches the analogue week exactly (research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues.all_weekly_moves['2026-01-26'] = -0.1204, the Q4 2025 earnings week)

jumps.name: Macao concession / Singapore licence impairment
jumps.reason: LVS operates on one of six Macao gaming concessions (renewed to Dec 2032) and one of two Singapore casino licences (duopoly protected to Jan 2031, 30-year concession from Aug 2006); the evaluation's core invalidation triggers include early revocation, material amendment, or non-renewal of either licence, which the note identifies as the central moat and the central risk if lost.
jumps.cite: research/LVS/2026-10-08-evaluation.md trigger: 'Macao concession (due Dec 2032) or Singapore license ... is revoked, materially amended, or not renewed ahead of schedule'; research/LVS/2026-10-08.md §2 (licence scarcity, SEC 10-K source)

annual_probability.cite: No Macao or Singapore concession/licence has been revoked or materially amended during the 5-year history underlying research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues; set to a low but nonzero tail probability given no observed base rate to count

impact.cite: Capped at the ±30% assumed-jump bound ([montecarlo] max_jump_impact_assumed in the project config) since no historical analogue exists for this risk

jumps.assumption: No historical analogue: no Macao/Singapore concession has been revoked or materially amended in the 5-year price history used for the jump-analogue table (research/LVS/2026-10-08-mc-inputs.json analogues), so impact is capped at the ±30% assumed-jump bound rather than taken from an observed week.
